name: Yamaji 2025, one Josephson parametric oscillator (JPO L), zero detuning
question: With the pump raised as t^5 over 100 ns and a one-photon bias raised linearly with it, which oscillation state does the oscillator lock to, and with what error against the bias power?
assumptions: Units: the total photon loss rate kappa_aL = 2 pi (0.75 + 0.31) MHz = 6.66e6 per second is 1; time in units of 1/kappa (150 ns).
Kerr: the paper writes (K_j/2) a†a†aa with K_L/2 pi = -12.6 MHz, so K = |K_L|/2 = 2 pi 6.3 MHz = 5.9 kappa.
Pump: p_L/2 pi = 148 MHz, so p = 140 kappa; the two-photon drive rises as (t/t_s)^5 over t_s = 100 ns = 0.666/kappa, i.e. the sweep variable s = t/t_s runs from 0 to 1 at the rate 1.5 kappa.

Bias: the one-photon drive rises linearly over the same 100 ns (slope exponent 1); its plateau amplitude h = Omega_dL/kappa is set from the signal power by Omega = sqrt(P kappa_eL/(hbar omega_r)) with kappa_eL/2 pi = 0.75 MHz and omega_r/2 pi = 9.88 GHz; the bias is assumed to push the amplified quadrature (the paper's optimal signal phase), which may differ from the paper's geometry by a factor cos(angle), i.e. by up to 3 dB in power.
Zero detuning throughout (the measurement without frequency chirping at Delta = 0); pure dephasing gamma_L/2 pi = 6.8 kHz = 0.0064 kappa as a dissipator on the photon number.
The one-photon drive is switched off 200 ns after the start of the ramp (its 100 ns rise plus its 100 ns plateau, Table I), i.e. at t = 1.333/kappa; the two-photon drive stays on.
The hold of 2/kappa = 300 ns brings the state to the start of the measurement window; the measurement integrates over the following 400 ns, which is not simulated.
Truncation at 44 quanta for stored states of about 12 photons.

provenance.reference: T. Yamaji et al., Quantum annealing in capacitively coupled Kerr parametric oscillators using frequency-chirped drives, Phys. Rev. Applied 24, 064052 (2025), arXiv:2506.23539v2: Eq. (B2), Appendix B (K, kappa, p, alpha), Appendix C and Table I (pulse sequence), Appendix E (dephasing 6.8 kHz), Fig. 3(d) and 4(b) (locking error against signal power)
